input.question: Friday Free-for-All | March 06, 2015
input.ground_truth: One of the atomic bomb questions that comes up on here quite often is whether anybody talked about "demonstrating" the atomic bomb before dropping it on Japan, and whether it was feasible. Well, I just posted a new blog post on this very subject: ["To demonstrate, or not to demonstrate?"](_URL_1_) It covers the history of this debate in 1945 in brief, and then speculates a little on the counterfactual dimensions. My conclusion is that while many of the common present-day objections to a demonstration are not very well-founded (e.g. they didn't have enough bombs to demonstrate one, it would have been hard to do, fallout would have been deadly anyway), ultimately I don't think a demonstration probably would have worked, and it probably would have got the US into even more problematic of a moral bind.
